1640: Infantry: Shield Cover (hold), Push. Spearmen: Spear Wall (stops trolls & cavalry), Javelins (instant heavy damage). Archers: Focused Volley, Fire Arrows (10s blaze). Cavalry: Flank Charge, Breakthrough. Whole army: Roar (attack ↑), Reform Lines (damage taken ↓). After use, the button shows the cooldown in seconds.
1642: Fury is full — press 4 to spin invincibly for a few seconds, sweeping away the Dead around you. Fury fills when you cut enemies, block right on time (B just before a hit), or roll out of the way at the last moment.
1644: Press Tab to open the big war map and slow time. Click or drag to select units, right-click to move or attack. Tab again to close.
1646: Battles led by a general are commanded from the overview. The general fights alongside the bodyguard on their own; press Q to use the general's ability.
1648: Generals read and block a repeated move. Mix slash, stab and skills; time a block (B) just before their attack and they stagger. Mash attacks and they counter without flinching.
1649: The realm's books — reading the top bar
1650: The +/day beside gold is the Palace's earnings (after soldiers' pay); the +/day beside food is the daily average including village tribute. Each village banks its share and sends it as tribute every three days. Soldiers eat 100 food a day per 2,000 at the Palace, or 150 per 1,000 on campaign. Click a village to see its daily income and banked tribute. People are the base for taxes and conscription; if favor reaches 0, the realm collapses. Short on gold? Borrow or trade food in Realm → Treasury.
1651: The king's horse is tied in the Palace yard — walk up and press E to ride, E again to dismount. On horseback you cross the big castle much faster.
1653: At the Forge (E), upgrade the king's sword and armor level by level — HP and damage go up (higher prowess unlocks the next level). In the Great Hall's wardrobe, change into armors unlocked by prowess, armor level, tournaments and renown.
1655: Realm → Treasury tab: borrow gold from the merchants' guild (10% interest a day) or sell surplus food to grain traders. Haggle in person at the market to sell for more.
1656: When the king visits in person
1657: Walk to the barracks, archery range, stables, chapel, market, farm or housing and press E — the 'King's Visit' does what the Realm window can't: instantly drill a company (★), sell food at a better price, boost the harvest, raise favor. Once a day per building.
1659: From the title screen or Settings, 'Battle practice' jumps straight into a battle scene. Your current game stays saved as it is.
1661: If the people drop below 300 or favor hits 0, the realm falls (game over). Guard your food, and raise favor with festivals, blessings and victories.
1672: Deploy (drag units into position, formation) → battle starts → without orders, units go after enemies they counter. Turn the tide with the unit command bar and the king's (or general's) blade.
1673: Commanding by type (5–9, G H J K)
1674: 5 infantry, 6 spearmen, 7 archers, 8 cavalry, 9 whole army. Press a number and those units glow with Commanding on their cards. G charge, H retreat, J first skill, K second skill go only to the commanded type. You can also press the buttons on the cards.
1679: Right-click slash, R stab, Ctrl roll, B block (just before a hit = parry → counter ×2), 1 whirlwind, 2 roar, 3 dash, 4 Rampage (when fury is full). Slash in rhythm for faster, stronger combos. You can't push through enemy soldiers.
1680: Battles led by a general are commanded only from the overview. The general fights with the bodyguard on their own; Q uses the general's ability. Only in battles the king leads in person does V switch to the king's view.
1682: Opens the big war map and slows time. Click or drag to select units, right-click to move or attack. V for the overview.
1683: The Palace has a half-ring wall (backed by the keep and mountains); villages have a ring palisade all around. Archers shoot from the walls (they climb back up if they come down; archer retreat = back to the wall). Infantry and spearmen on the wall throw stones. If the gate breaks, the enemy pours through it.
1685: Defenders have a big advantage in a castle. Infantry are the heroes — under their shields they climb ladders fastest and fall least, then shove forward once over. A group of spearmen rams the gate, two catapults break the walls. Archers outside only hit the wall top and just inside. Cavalry wait until there's a breach, then pour in. The Dead on the walls throw firepots and bone spears.
1687: Archers on the wall only shoot outward in front of them — the far side of the castle is hidden behind the walls. With no visible enemies, they move along the wall toward the enemy. Spread evenly they cover every side but each spot is weaker; bunch them up and another side empties, letting the Dead come over ladders there.
1689: Trolls lead, and the rest of the Dead hide behind them, marching in step — when the trolls hit or reach the wall, they all surge at once. Bring trolls down first with archers and javelins. At walls, trolls break one section, orcs and wolves batter the gate, and ghouls and goblins climb ladders (archers holding the wall knock them off). Break the Dead's catapults by opening the gate and sending out cavalry. The Lord of the Dead (Claude) picks a tactic each battle and remembers past fights. Scouts announce the tactic about 7s in. Great Raids are announced three days ahead with their composition and direction.
1690: From the title screen or Settings, Battle practice lets you jump into a field battle, fort assault, Palace defense or elite trial. Your current game stays as it is.
1692: Generals read and block a repeated move, and counter without flinching if you just mash. Mix slash, stab and block.
1696: Epilogue — rebuilding goals
1697: Renown +2 for each one. Achieve them all to become the Restorer King.
1698:
How to win — Act I
Ch.1 Prepare (7 days) → Ch.2 one fort → Ch.3 three forts → Ch.4 Throne of the Dead (opens when three forts fall, or on day 50). Defeat the King of the Dead on the throne to complete Act I.
How to lose
If the people fall below 300 or favor reaches 0, the realm falls. Lose a Palace defense and you lose 35% of the people, half the gold and 40% of the food. If the Dead come while there's no garrison at all, the Palace is plundered without a fight.
1699:
Great Raids
From day 20, every 20 days, a great host comes for the Palace. A herald warns three days ahead. The more forts you raze, the smaller they get.
